implementation.name: JTTORA
implementation.notes: Source availability (T5.4): open -- the HDL lives in the jotego/jtcores monorepo at cores/tora/, 12 source files. There is no open_source column in the delivered schema (data-model.md §1.9 deleted the proposed core table together with its flags); the presence of hdl_language_id, license_id and implementation_path rows is how that fact is stated here. License: https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/blob/master/LICENSE is the verbatim GPLv3 text, and the per-file grant in https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/blob/master/cores/tora/hdl/jttora_adpcm.v reads "either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version" -- hence GPL-3.0-or-later. Machine mapping: 4 MRA files in jotego/jtbin's mra/ directory name <rbf>jttora</rbf>; 2 setnames resolved exactly to a MAME 0.288 machine and 2 through MAME's own cloneof relation to the parent that survives extract/machine.json's parents-only filter, giving 2 distinct machine_id rows. hdl_language_id: 12 of 12 HDL files are verilog (12 verilog), excluding the shared framework directory. accuracy_id omitted: jotego's README claims faithfulness in prose but states no timing-fidelity level this build could check against data/lookup/accuracy_level.json. The mirror-image relationship is recorded here rather than on jtbiocom: this core's cores/tora/cfg/files.yaml pulls jtbiocom_main.v and jtbiocom_mcu.v (headers Date: 12-9-2019 and 14-9-2019) out of cores/biocom/hdl, three years older than this core's own jttora_obj.v, so Tiger Road reuses Bionic Commando's 68000 and 8751 main section and that is the direction recorded. cores/biocom/cfg/files.yaml pulls this core's object engine back the other way, but that is shared-module reuse, not JTBIOCOM consuming JTTORA, and writing it would close a dependency cycle.
